how: Participants propose a fandom mark and explicitly call members to help place it.
Short work reports, thanks, and bare assent answer participation and assistance proposals.
A participant makes a tiny tribute, while other participants propose and locate the larger fandom mark.
Joining through recognition is the narrator's explanation of collective completion, so attributing that joining to a room call requires evidence of an intervening call.
Participants choose logo colors and revise toward a realistic goal before further d20 and logo proposals reopen the design.
Participants report the completed triangle and difficulty holding it, while another participant contests its attribution.
Coordinates, a requested grid, an offered template, and replacement instructions make individual placements more mutually intelligible.
A created tribute receives repair and repeated checking on each pixel cooldown.
The group explicitly turns to defense and endorses preserving the existing work over expansion because greed could undo it.
A helper admits undoing planned expansion because it looked like vandalism, directly fitting the revised mistaken-repair mechanism.
Mistaken repair is established, but permanent loss or abandonment caused by failed communication requires evidence beyond the admission and later permission and template instructions.
A helper attributes interference to their own defensive action after misreading expansion as vandalism.
Participants refuse to dig into others' spaces, urge restraint, and protect neighbors who helped.
A collision request receives an agreed leftward adjustment, and a later compromise receives acceptance of minimal overlap.
An instruction to take a colored strip and a proposal to exploit an attacked neighbor show encroachment or its proposal without establishing a coordinated raid.
A realistic revised goal does not establish relocation following erasure or overrun.
Completion announcements, congratulations, reflection, and credit-giving mark the work as a collective achievement.
An explicit end announcement records that the work is intact, alongside a participant's recollection of vigilant watching.
The coded journey reflection and congratulations do not establish a decision to carry the effort forward.
Cooldown watching and vigilant defense do not establish whether other participants used scripts, bots, or spare accounts.
Announced assistance receives thanks and a reciprocal promise to protect the helpers' territory.
Participants report a communal alliance Discord invitation and conversation with neighboring groups there.
Triangle ownership jokes are followed by a late rival-directed claim of failure.
Permission to cross a flag and assistance from a neighbor do not establish a guest work under continuing host rule.
The host applies its spoiler-tag posting requirement to a canvas proposal.
Accepting overlap and requesting retreat do not explicitly dispute or state limits on who can commit the room.
A late triangle taunt and an unchallenged contribution account do not establish contest over a preserved canvas version or historical account.
Moderators reveal an appreciation-post parody, participants extend it, and further appreciation is routed into that thread.
Members interpret the changed banner through date and time-zone explanations, enjoy and share it, and complain about illegible navigation.
Struggling to hold a triangle and judging the desired build impossible express limits on the effort.
Contested triangle attribution does not establish a quarrel predating the canvas.
An existing fandom uses its logo, member name, and a d20 as recognizable cues for shared work.
Template instructions and reported Discord coordination do not establish whether participants decided offices, voting, sanctions, or divisions of labor.
A neighbor already being attacked supplies the stated opportunity for expansion without a cited prior tie motivating it.
A participant relays a neighbor's promise to negotiate further work without establishing a formal representative office.
A reply reports an all-day attempt already underway, so the preceding teamwork post cannot be assumed to have initiated that placing.
The Natural 20 narrator explains joining through recognition of a lone start, so an intervening recruitment call must be evidenced rather than supplied by the model.
A tiny tribute is followed by repair and repeated cooldown checks.
Construction collisions already initiate border negotiation before the explicit defense turn, requiring a route from building as well as upkeep.
Restraint is explicitly justified by protecting helpers and avoiding destructive greed, so a settled border alone does not explain the local choice.
Vigilance and conflicting templates establish neither machine hands nor their introduction because upkeep exceeded manual capacity.
Completion announcements celebrate the work as finished.
Celebration precedes recording the intact ending, but the concepts do not establish that celebration caused that record.
The ending and journey reflection do not establish a continuation decision or its dependence on recording.
Feasibility doubts and a realistic revised goal do not establish insufficient defenders causing relocation following a documented loss.
A new template precedes a later report of two-link conflict, so posting settles design only if participants converge on the current version.
A direct request to seek outside help receives bare assent, supporting this pair without testing the broader comparison between acceptance and refusal.
Outside help arrives during construction before the explicit defense turn, so assistance need not originate in upkeep strain.
The border request and incoming help involve different parties, so their order does not establish one exchange causing the other.
Recruitment precedes opportunistic expansion, but the concepts do not establish that the initial call caused those expansion proposals.
An appeal for peace receives an opportunistic counterproposal, so restraint does not always follow and answer an attack call.
An expansion instruction precedes reported permission, but the cited concepts do not establish aggression causing the permission exchange.
Triangle taunts are not demonstrably caused by a particular attack, especially when the separately coded strip expansion concerns another setting.
Coalition invitation follows defense, but its wording does not establish a shared attack as the reason for joining.
The removal applies an ordinary spoiler-tag requirement rather than establishing new canvas containment caused by a flood of calls.
The compromise exchange supplies no authority limit or refusal of commitment with which to test the newly bounded transition.
Explicit parody conveys a genuine moderation request to reduce repetitive appreciation posts.
Instructions coordinate builders only insofar as participants recognize the current template and distinguish planned expansion from damage.
Convergence requires superseding conflicting template links rather than merely adding another version.
A neighbor's collision request prompts an explicit change in the intended direction of the build.
A peacekeeping refusal receives an opportunistic expansion counterproposal, establishing a reverse response sequence alongside restraint efforts.
Celebrating completed lettering is followed by d20 and logo proposals, so a finished stage can reopen design work.
The call to action is relayed into an existing Discord, while later reports return neighbor conversation from that venue.
Participants ask for a canvas link and progress information and identify the picture claimed as a triangle.
An allied contributor enters through joint work and receives thanks, without establishing subscriber growth or sustained integration into ordinary room activity.
Participants make a new joke from competing claims to the same triangle.
Builders choose coordinates and agree to extend left to avoid a neighbor's work before any documented loss.
Calling an existing fandom and relaying its recruitment into Discord do not establish a new room formed around a canvas pattern.
Refusing to dig into others' work does not establish a dispute about offensive language, slurs, or hate symbols.
Choosing a fandom logo and congratulating builders do not establish efforts to secure creators' or press attention.
An argument for keeping peace receives an opportunistic counterproposal, while another exchange favors defense because greed could undo the work.
Competing templates and uncertainty about coordination do not establish a personal quarrel, withdrawal under strain, or interpersonal repair.
Relaying recruitment to Discord and reporting neighbor conversation establish neither secrecy nor infiltration.
Mistakenly undoing expansion as vandalism does not establish hostility to canvas posts motivating deliberate destruction of the room's own work.
One member fits checking to each pixel cooldown, while another later recalls intensive vigilance without quantifying its personal cost.
An ordinary cooldown and a normal end announcement do not evidence site faults or workarounds.
Help between groups and concern about an overlapping worm do not establish a speaker's dual membership or divided loyalty.
